message.content:
Pantone doesn’t publish a single “official” code called *Sky Blue*, so designers usually pick from several close‑matching hues depending on the desired brightness and saturation. Here are three commonly referenced Pantone values that people use when they say “sky blue”:

| # | Pantone Code | Description / Notes |
|---|--------------|---------------------|
| **A** | **PMS 15–3920 C** | A bright, slightly turquoise‑tinted sky blue often seen in fashion & branding. |
| **B** | **PMS 14–4318 C** | Slightly cooler than A, more muted – good for corporate palettes where you want a calm feel. |
| **C** | **PMS 12–5902 C** | Very light, almost pastel sky blue—great for airy interiors or soft graphic design. |

If you’re working off a physical Pantone swatch book, look under the “Cool Blues” section around those numbers. If you only have digital software, most programs let you enter the PMS value directly (e.g., `PMS 15-3920`).

> **Tip:** Because Pantone’s system changes over time (new editions, updated inks), it’s always best to confirm the exact match against a current Pantone Color Bridge guide or a calibrated monitor/print proof whenever possible.
